rules.statement: When a change adds or renames a field or event in a documented record or wire contract, update the contract document in the same change.
rules.why: The document is the reviewed contract that log pipelines, trace backends and runbooks are built against, so the code and the document must not drift apart.
rules.check: A diff that adds or renames a record field, a field-name constant or an event name without touching the corresponding contract documentation.

rules.statement: Audit and log records must carry identifiers and metadata only, never a token, an authorization code, a credential, a secret or a query string.
rules.why: Audit records are forwarded to log pipelines and trace backends, and secrets must not leak there.
rules.check: Audit details, error messages, log state or span tags that include token values, codes, secrets, passwords or the raw request query string or full URL.

rules.statement: When recording a request's path in audit or telemetry data, use PathBase plus Path and never include the query string.
rules.why: The query string can carry authorization codes or tokens.
rules.check: Use of Request.QueryString, GetDisplayUrl, GetEncodedUrl or a full URI when filling a recorded request path.

rules.statement: Model vocabularies such as outcomes, severities, categories, sources and resource types as open sets of lower-case string names, not enumerations, unless the set is provably closed.
rules.why: Under ADR-0150, a package that adds an event must be able to add its own names without editing the core library.
rules.check: A new enum, or a closed switch that rejects unknown values, used for an extensible vocabulary; vocabulary names that are not lower-case.

rules.statement: Metric attributes must carry only bounded-cardinality values, never identifiers or free-form names.
rules.why: Metrics carry only the bounded fields (event name, category, outcome); unbounded values such as IDs or free-form environment names break the counters.
rules.check: Metric tags or attributes built from IDs, user names, client IDs, paths or free-form names such as an environment_name.

rules.statement: Use the same field names for one concept across the structured record, the log state, span tags and metric attributes, changing only a namespace prefix, and declare those names as shared constants.
rules.why: An operator can then move between a log entry, its trace and the counters without translating names.
rules.check: Hard-coded string literals for record or tag names, or a log, span or metric name that differs from the record's field name apart from its prefix.

rules.statement: In a serialized audit record, leave out any member that has no value, and any empty array, instead of writing null or [].
rules.why: The record contract says absent members are omitted and never written as null.
rules.check: Writer code that calls WriteNull or writes an empty array for an absent audit member.

rules.statement: Bump the minor schema version of a versioned record envelope whenever a field is added to it.
rules.why: Consumers rely on schema_version to know which fields to expect.
rules.check: A diff that adds a field to the record writer without changing the schema version constant.

rules.statement: Generate audit event identifiers as UUIDv7 and write event timestamps as RFC 3339 in UTC with a 'Z' suffix.
rules.why: UUIDv7 identifiers sort by time, which helps indexing and pagination, and a fixed UTC format keeps the contract consistent.
rules.check: Use of Guid.NewGuid() for event IDs, or timestamps written with a local offset or in a non-RFC 3339 format.

rules.statement: Truncate caller-supplied header values such as User-Agent to a fixed maximum length (512 characters) before recording them.
rules.why: The contract cuts the User-Agent at 512 characters, so untrusted input cannot inflate records.
rules.check: A User-Agent or similar header copied into audit or telemetry data without truncation.

rules.statement: Give each audit error a stable, machine-readable code (the OAuth error code where one applies), and keep secrets out of the human-readable message.
rules.why: Operators filter and pivot on the code, and the message is forwarded to log sinks.
rules.check: Error codes built from free text or exception messages, or error messages that interpolate secrets or credentials.

rules.statement: Derive an audit entry's log level from its severity: Information for info and for unknown severities, Warning for warning, Critical for critical. Severity defaults to warning on failure and to info otherwise.
rules.why: The contract makes the log level follow the severity, so alerting stays consistent.
rules.check: An audit log written at a hard-coded level that ignores severity, or an unknown severity that is not mapped to Information.
